nodes.label: Active Inference
nodes.rationale: Treated as a direct corollary of the FEP: action and perception differ only in direction, and Expected Free Energy splits into epistemic (ambiguity reduction) and instrumental (risk minimization) terms, unifying exploration and exploitation.

nodes.label: World Models for Autonomous Driving (Wayve)
nodes.rationale: Learns a latent representation of road scenes from fleet data so driving policies can be evaluated closed-loop, because real-world testing is expensive and dangerous.

nodes.label: Causal World Models
nodes.rationale: Distinguishing intervention from observation is the step needed for genuine counterfactual 'what if?' reasoning, judged the most promising direction.

nodes.label: CURL (Contrastive Unsupervised Representations)
nodes.rationale: Uses instance discrimination to shape the latent space without a generative decoder, avoiding the computational cost of reconstructing high-dimensional observations.

nodes.label: Dorsal and Ventral Streams
nodes.rationale: Cited as the biological precedent for separating representational ('what') from spatial ('where/how') pathways in modern world model architectures.

nodes.label: DreamerV2
nodes.rationale: Discrete categorical latents with straight-through gradients give richer multimodal representations; KL balancing and two-hot reward prediction fight posterior collapse and improve value learning.

nodes.label: DreamerV3
nodes.rationale: Targets one hyperparameter set across hundreds of domains: symlog transforms handle varying target scale without normalization, free bits keep the posterior from collapsing, and running-statistic-normalized heads enable cross-domain transfer.

nodes.label: Free Energy Principle (FEP)
nodes.rationale: Makes world models a thermodynamic necessity: minimizing variational free energy is an upper bound on sensory surprise, so perception becomes variational inference over a generative model.

nodes.label: Generative World Models
nodes.rationale: Model the full joint distribution so novel trajectories can be sampled; the gain is environment simulation, the cost is high computational sample cost.

nodes.label: Google Genie
nodes.rationale: Learns an explicit latent action space from unannotated video via a video tokenizer plus causal dynamics model, so a single prompt image can instantiate a controllable interactive 2D world at inference.

nodes.label: IRIS
nodes.rationale: Replaces recurrent memory with a GPT-style transformer over VQ-VAE tokens, gaining sample efficiency competitive with model-free methods while keeping discrete token capacity.

nodes.label: High-Capacity Video Generation Models (GAIA-1, UniSim)
nodes.rationale: Treated historically as media synthesis, but implicitly learn intuitive physics, object permanence and temporal causality from raw pixels.

nodes.label: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
nodes.rationale: The primary application: hallucinated rollouts raise sample efficiency by orders of magnitude and ensembles of world models supply uncertainty estimates for exploration.

nodes.label: Planning in Latent Space
nodes.rationale: Rolls candidate action sequences out in latent space to avoid expensive pixel-level simulation, then executes only the first action.

nodes.label: Predictive Coding
nodes.rationale: Only residual prediction errors are propagated upward instead of raw sensory states, which is what maps onto self-supervised learning signals in RSSMs and Predictive Coding Networks.

nodes.label: Predictive World Models
nodes.rationale: Learn a transition dynamics function for forecasting; the weakness is susceptibility to representation collapse, the strength is cheap latent look-ahead planning.

nodes.label: RSSM (Recurrent State-Space Model)
nodes.rationale: Hybrid state: the deterministic path carries long-range temporal dependencies while the stochastic path captures multimodal outcomes, which avoids the posterior collapse of purely stochastic recurrent models.

nodes.label: VAE Vision Component (V)
nodes.rationale: Compresses high-dimensional observations into a compact latent representation so all downstream prediction and control happens in latent space instead of pixels.

nodes.label: Valor autograd class
nodes.rationale: Stores data plus grad and builds the computational graph dynamically via operator overloading; each op defines a local _backward closure, so any differentiable function composes from a small set of primitives.

nodes.label: BatchNorm class
nodes.rationale: Learnable gamma/beta let the layer recover the identity if normalization would destroy useful signal; an EMA of batch statistics is kept because a single batch's statistics at inference are unreliable (hence model.eval()).

nodes.label: Dropout class
nodes.rationale: Prevents co-adaptation by forcing redundant representations; the mask is scaled by 1/(1-p) at training time (inverted dropout) so inference needs no scaling and keeps the expected output magnitude.

nodes.label: Adam (Adaptive Moment Estimation)
nodes.rationale: Combines momentum (first moment) and RMSProp (second moment) with bias correction; the correction is needed because m_t and v_t start at zero and would otherwise make early updates far too small, slowing the start of training.

nodes.label: Computational Graph (DAG)
nodes.rationale: Expressions are represented as a DAG of operations so the chain rule can be applied automatically instead of by hand: forward pass evaluates leaves to root and caches values, backward pass walks the same graph in reverse.

nodes.label: Forward-Mode Autodiff (Dual Numbers)
nodes.rationale: Attaching a dual number x + x_dot*eps propagates one directional derivative per pass, so a full gradient over n parameters costs n forward passes — hopeless for networks with millions of parameters.

nodes.label: Learning Rate
nodes.rationale: Too large overshoots the valley and diverges (each step lands higher on the opposite slope); too small wastes compute — hence schedules or adaptive per-parameter rates.

nodes.label: Mini-Batch SGD
nodes.rationale: Balances the low-variance estimate of batch gradient descent with the GPU throughput of batched matrix multiplications; batch size controls the gradient noise level.

nodes.label: Momentum Optimizer
nodes.rationale: Accumulating velocity makes perpendicular (zig-zag) components cancel while the down-ravine component grows, fixing plain SGD's oscillation in ravines; gamma ~0.9 is a robust default.

nodes.label: Reverse-Mode Autodiff
nodes.rationale: Chosen for deep learning because the network has millions of inputs (parameters) and a single scalar output: one forward plus one backward pass yields the derivative with respect to every input at O(graph size) cost.

nodes.label: RMSProp Optimizer
nodes.rationale: Divides the step by a moving average of squared gradients, shrinking the effective rate of parameters with consistently large gradients and normalizing step sizes across the network; eps prevents division by zero.

nodes.label: Multivariable Chain Rule (Sum Rule)
nodes.rationale: A parameter that reaches the loss along multiple paths must receive the gradient contribution of every path; this is why autograd accumulates with += instead of assignment. Overwriting would drop gradient paths and yield incorrect updates.

nodes.label: Training Loop
nodes.rationale: Gradients must be zeroed before each backward pass because they accumulate by design (sum rule); otherwise gradients from previous steps pile up and updates overshoot.

nodes.label: Vector-Jacobian Product (VJP)
nodes.rationale: Materializing full Jacobians is infeasible, so autograd only needs each op to multiply an incoming gradient vector by its Jacobian; for elementwise ops the Jacobian is diagonal and the VJP is an elementwise product.

nodes.label: L2 Regularization (Weight Decay)
nodes.rationale: Equivalent to MAP estimation with a Gaussian prior over weights; the penalty adds lambda*w to the gradient so weights decay by (1 - eta*lambda) each step, preferring distributed small weights over a few dominant ones.

nodes.label: Regularization
nodes.rationale: Any technique that reduces generalization error, usually at the cost of increased training error, by constraining the hypothesis space.

nodes.label: Cross-Entropy Loss
nodes.rationale: Punishes a confident-but-wrong prediction exponentially, forcing the network to learn class boundaries quickly instead of settling on timid predictions.

nodes.label: The Learn Paradigm
nodes.rationale: Instead of a human writing rules, data and answers are supplied and the algorithm searches for the rules; this requires a hypothesis space, a loss function and an optimization algorithm.

nodes.label: Mean Squared Error
nodes.rationale: Squaring keeps the error positive and penalizes large errors disproportionately, pushing the network to fix its worst mistakes first.

nodes.label: Topological Sort
nodes.rationale: A node is processed only after all its children, so by iterating in reverse topological order the incoming gradient (out.grad) is fully accumulated before local gradients are computed.

nodes.label: Early Stopping
nodes.rationale: Halting when validation loss starts to rise constrains the optimizer's trajectory in weight space, landing in a wider, flatter minimum that generalizes better than a sharp deep one.

nodes.label: Inductive Bias
nodes.rationale: No model can learn without assumptions: a small hypothesis space is easy to optimize but fails on complex relationships, while a vast one needs vast data to avoid mere memorization.

nodes.label: Diffusion Models
nodes.rationale: Splits generation into a fixed forward noising process and a learned reverse denoising chain, trading much higher sampling cost for training stability and better sample quality than GANs or VAEs.

nodes.label: Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)
nodes.rationale: Two models compete in a zero-sum game so the generator never needs an explicit likelihood; the trade-off is instability and mode collapse, which motivated the alternative losses listed for WGAN/LSGAN.

nodes.label: Gram Matrix
nodes.rationale: Inner products between vectorized feature maps capture co-occurrence of features, i.e. texture, while being invariant to spatial arrangement, which is what makes style separable from content.

nodes.label: Non-Saturating Heuristic
nodes.rationale: Reformulating the generator loss avoids weak gradients when the discriminator easily rejects samples; the cost is that it no longer has the same theoretical basis as minimizing the Jensen-Shannon divergence.

nodes.label: Reparameterization Trick
nodes.rationale: Sampling z from q(z|x) is stochastic and non-differentiable; sampling epsilon from a fixed base distribution and transforming it keeps the graph differentiable so gradient descent still works.

nodes.label: Stable Diffusion
nodes.rationale: Running diffusion in a pretrained VAE latent space instead of pixel space cuts compute and sampling time and lets the diffusion model focus on high-level semantics while the VAE handles low-level detail.

nodes.label: Style Transfer
nodes.rationale: Uses a pretrained CNN as a hierarchical feature extractor: deep layers encode content (objects/forms), shallow-to-mid layers encode style (textures/color/patterns), so one network can separate the two signals.

nodes.label: U-Net
nodes.rationale: Skip connections between the contracting and expanding paths preserve fine details while still capturing multi-scale context, which is why it predicts the noise well at every diffusion step.

nodes.label: Variational Autoencoder (VAE)
nodes.rationale: Models a probability distribution over the latent space instead of a deterministic code, which is what enables sampling and generation and makes the latent space smooth enough to interpolate.

nodes.label: Long-Horizon Prediction
nodes.rationale: Compounding error makes long rollouts degrade quadratically; proposed fixes are iterative refinement, sparse temporal attention and hierarchical timescale separation.

nodes.label: MLP class (Valor-based)
nodes.rationale: The network is built the same way as any expression, so calling the model performs the forward pass and silently constructs the graph; parameters() collects exactly the leaves whose gradients backpropagation will fill.

nodes.label: Activation Functions
nodes.rationale: Without a nonlinearity, stacking layers collapses into a single linear transformation W2(W1 x) = W'x; activations bend and fold the space so complex decision boundaries become representable.

nodes.label: Artificial Neuron (Perceptron)
nodes.rationale: A single neuron is an affine transformation plus a non-linearity; geometrically the weights define a hyperplane, so it can only represent linearly separable functions.

nodes.label: Hebbian Theory / Synaptic Plasticity
nodes.rationale: Neurons that fire together, wire together: adaptive connection strengths in biology are the direct inspiration for learning by adjusting artificial weights.

nodes.label: Multilayer Perceptron (MLP)
nodes.rationale: Layers are computed with matrix operations so all neurons of a layer are evaluated at once; stacking layers is what makes non-linearly-separable problems like XOR solvable.

nodes.label: Universal Approximation Theorem
nodes.rationale: Guarantees an MLP with enough neurons can approximate any continuous function, but says nothing about how to find the parameters — capacity is not the same as trainability.

nodes.label: Bias-Variance Decomposition
nodes.rationale: Splits expected squared error into Bias^2 (wrong assumptions, underfitting), Variance (sensitivity to training-set fluctuations, overfitting) and irreducible noise; classical practice sought the capacity minimizing their sum.

nodes.label: Double Descent
nodes.rationale: Past the interpolation threshold, hugely over-parameterized models see test error drop again: they seek the simplest function interpolating the data, which is why billion-parameter LLMs do not catastrophically overfit.

nodes.label: Empirical Risk vs Expected Risk
nodes.rationale: The true distribution is unavailable, so we minimize the error over the training dataset as a proxy for the expected risk over all data.
